_note: Hand-written. The canonical forgotten thread. The promise is deliberately one clean quotable sentence so the forgotten agent has something to point at, and so the share card has a candidate. Three inbound, one outbound, then nothing. His last message gives her an easy exit she never takes, which is worse than if he had been annoyed. Depends on the two April peer threads existing first, so the ask reads as one friend asking another rather than a stranger emailing a resource.
subject: a favor, and please say no if it's weird

messages.subject: a favor, and please say no if it's weird
messages.body:
Feel free to say no to this and I will never bring it up again.

We're putting together a small pre-seed, and Marguerite Vance keeps coming up as the one person who actually understands the operator side of what we're building. I saw she led yours. Would you be up for making an introduction?

I know intros are a real thing to spend, and you just closed, so if the answer is "not right now" or "not yet" or "ask me in six months," all of those are completely fine answers and I mean it.

Either way, congratulations on the round. I saw the announcement and I was genuinely thrilled for you.

J

messages.subject: Re: a favor, and please say no if it's weird
messages.body:
Happy to. Let me think about the right framing so it actually lands, she gets a lot of these and the ones that work are specific about why her in particular.

Give me a few days.

Best,
Priya

messages.subject: Re: a favor, and please say no if it's weird
messages.body:
No pressure at all, just floating this back up.

Did you get a chance to think about the framing? Happy to write a draft blurb you can edit or throw away entirely, if that turns it into a two-minute thing instead of a twenty-minute thing.

Also, glad the Corbin call was useful. He told me you asked him about front desk turnover for forty minutes, which is apparently the first time a founder has asked him anything he actually knows about.

J

messages.subject: Re: a favor, and please say no if it's weird
messages.body:
Last time I'll bring this up, promise.

If it's not a fit, or the timing is bad, or you thought about it and landed on no, genuinely no hard feelings. I'd just rather know than keep wondering whether my email went to spam.

Hope Thicket is going well. The scheduling stuff looked really good in the demo you sent back in April.

J
